name: agent-resumption
context: Long-running agent tasks that must survive process restarts, container redeployments, user disconnects, or infrastructure events without losing meaningful work. State is checkpointed to durable storage so the agent can resume from a named boundary rather than retrying from scratch or duplicating side effects.
benefits: Agents survive infrastructure events (restarts, deploys, crashes) without losing progress
Prevents duplicate side effects (double emails, double charges) through idempotency keys
Enables long-running tasks that would otherwise be impractical in stateless environments
Provides a natural pause point for human review or escalation
tradeoffs: Checkpoint storage cost accumulates with run duration and state size
Resumed runs may encounter drifted external state (external systems changed during pause)
Non-serializable in-memory references are forbidden in long-running paths
Requires idempotency guarantees from all downstream side-effect targets
use_cases: Research scraping: a 40-minute scrape-and-summarize run survives a container restart
Code migration: a multi-hour refactoring task resumes after a deployment
Customer service: an agent handling a complex multi-turn ticket pauses for human review, then resumes
Batch processing: a large document set is processed across restarts without reprocessing completed items
avoid_when: Tasks complete in seconds — retry-from-scratch is cheaper
Downstream services cannot make their operations idempotent
State is inherently ephemeral and retrying from scratch is acceptable
anti_patterns: Keeping all state in memory with no durable checkpoint — loses work on any interruption
Checkpointing at arbitrary points rather than meaningful boundaries
Resuming without revalidating external state that may have drifted
Resuming without classifying ambiguous timeouts as ToolOutcomeUnknown — blind continuation re-fires side effects
design_principles: Agent state must be serializable — no in-memory function references
Checkpoints must occur at named boundaries (not mid-step) for consistent resumption
Every side-effect target must accept an idempotency key to prevent duplicates on replay
Write idempotency key before network call; record result before advancing step
Resume tokens with epoch prevent stale workers from resuming after lease expiry
best_practices: Checkpoint at goal milestones, not at arbitrary iteration counts
Distinguish durable state (keep across restarts) from ephemeral state (recompute)
Validate that resumed runs re-check volatile external state (queue positions, approvals)
references: Wu et al., Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes, 2026 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.28138
Agent Patterns Catalog, Agent Resumption pattern — https://www.agentpatternscatalog.org/patterns/agent-resumption/
